newsitem.title: UK: British shares jump after Bank of England reforms.
newsitem.headline: British shares jump after Bank of England reforms.

text.p: The British blue chip FTSE 100 index surged to new record highs Tuesday after the new Chancellor Gordon Brown made an early move to raise interest rates and unexpectedly gave the central bank independence to set interest rate policy.

UK shares had pared opening gains on caution ahead of the announcement after the regular monthly monetary meeting between the government and the Bank of England was suddenly brought forward by one day.
The FTSE had pushed through the 4,500 level for the first time as the market opened, taking its lead from a blistering rally in the U.S.
By 1140 GMT the FTSE was up 65.7 pts at 4,521.3. Just before the announcement of the quarter point rise in official interest rates, the index was up just 18.6.
"Everyone was expecting a 25 basis point rise and that's what they got, the gilt market should certainly like this," said Steve Wright, BZW UK equity strategist.
"But the key thing now is an indication of when the mini-budget is going to be...the market really needs to know."
UK June gilt futures jumped more than two points to set a contract high and FTSE index futures led the way for equities.
"The (equity) futures had sold off ahead of this news on worries that the rate rise might be half a point and that would have been seen as overly agressive," said one futures specialist.

"If it's good for gilts it's going to be good for equities," said Mark Tinker, strategist at UBS. "Right now the same chartists who a few weeks ago were saying the FTSE could drop to 3,800 will probably now be talking about it going to 4,800."
Dealers said the surprise news that the new Labour government was giving the central bank operational independence to set interest rates had futher lifted sentiment.

"Giving more independence to the Bank of England to set interest rates is probably more significant than the fact that interest rates have gone up," said Wright at BZW. "It is a long way towards an independent central bank, which is a very euro-friendly policy."

Just two days into the new government, the leading FTSE index has responded with record performances, setting an intraday peak of 4,468.4 on Friday which was smashed after the Dow rose 143.29 points or two percent to a record 7,214.49.
But dealers said UK equities could still struggle to outperform other international markets ahead of concrete news on Labour's budget proposals, which are tipped to hit the corporate sector hard.

"They have ruled out a number of options already but there are still plenty of fiscal measures they could take on the personal and corporate taxation side," Wright said. "The market is beginning to warm to these ideas."
"The market has been hitting new highs but we are still underperforming the U.S. and other European markets," said Wright. "I'd much rather be betting on a rally in gilts."

Investors in the U.S. meanwhile, were becoming increasingly hopeful that inflation was being held in check, limiting the extent of a possible interest rate rise at the next FOMC meeting on May 20. "What's happening in the States is that there seems to be growth without too much pressure on inflation," a dealer said. "So people are only looking for a small rate rise."
Dealers expected the Dow to fall prey to profit-taking on Tuesday after gains of nearly three percent in the last two sessions.

Among London's big share movers was B.A.T Industries which jumped 17-1/2 pence to 539p after a U.S. court cleared tobacco giant R.J Reynolds of responsibility for the death of a smoker who died of lung cancer.
Oil giant BP leapt 27-1/2p to 731p after the company reported net earnings, before exceptional items of 755 million pounds ($1.2 billion), above analysts best expectations.
Glaxo led the drugs sector higher following a report that U.S. approval for a new anti-depressant could come within weeks. The shares jumped 20 pence to 12.13-1/2 pounds. ($ = 0.618 British Pounds)
